items.followUp: How does a pure substance differ from a mixture? Give one example of each.

rubric.why: A homogeneous mixture has the same composition throughout, and a valid example illustrates it.
rubric.description: Describes a homogeneous mixture as uniform throughout and gives a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining feature and an example such as salt solution, sugar solution, or air.

rubric.why: A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition, as shown by mixtures whose components are not evenly distributed.
rubric.description: Describes a heterogeneous mixture as non-uniform and gives a valid example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the defining feature and an example such as sand and water or oil and water.

modelAnswer: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout; for example, salt solution.
A heterogeneous mixture has a non-uniform composition throughout; for example, sand and water.

items.followUp: Find the empirical formula and molecular mass of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆.

rubric.why: The subscripts in acetic acid, C₂H₄O₂, reduce to the simplest whole-number ratio 1:2:1.
rubric.description: Gives the empirical formula of acetic acid.
Calculates the molecular mass of acetic acid and gives a suitable unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a molecular mass of 60 u.

modelAnswer: Acetic acid has molecular formula C₂H₄O₂; dividing the subscripts by 2 gives the empirical formula CH₂O.

items.followUp: Why do outer electrons experience less attraction from the nucleus when inner shells are occupied?

rubric.why: Bigger atoms generally have more occupied shells and therefore more inner electrons between the nucleus and outer electrons.
rubric.description: Relates larger atomic size to having more shells or energy levels and inner electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the greater number of shells or energy levels and inner electrons.

rubric.why: Inner electrons screen outer electrons from some of the nucleus’s attraction, increasing the shielding effect.
rubric.description: Explains that inner electrons shield or screen outer electrons from nuclear attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the shielding or screening by inner electrons.

modelAnswer: Bigger atoms have more electron shells, with more inner electrons.
These inner electrons shield the outer electrons from the full attraction of the nucleus, producing a greater shielding effect.
